questions.enonce_markdown:
A discrete random variable $X$ has probability mass function defined by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} c\,(9-x^2), & \text{for } x=1,\,2\\ c\,(25-x^2), & \text{for } x=3,\,4\\ 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

Find the value of the constant $c$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The probabilities must sum to $1$. The values of the bracket are

| $x$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bracket | $9-1=8$ | $9-4=5$ | $25-9=16$ | $25-16=9$ |

$$\sum f(x) = c(8+5+16+9) = 38c = 1 \;\Longrightarrow\; c = \frac{1}{38}.$$

questions.enonce_markdown: A discrete random variable $X$ has probability mass function $f(x)=c(9-x^2)$ for $x=1,2$, $f(x)=c(25-x^2)$ for $x=3,4$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. Find the median of $X$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $c=\dfrac1{38}$ the probabilities are $f(1)=\dfrac{8}{38}$, $f(2)=\dfrac{5}{38}$, $f(3)=\dfrac{16}{38}$, $f(4)=\dfrac{9}{38}$.

Cumulative probabilities:

$$P(X\le 1)=\frac{8}{38}\approx0.211,\qquad P(X\le 2)=\frac{13}{38}\approx0.342,\qquad P(X\le 3)=\frac{29}{38}\approx0.763.$$

The median is the smallest value $m$ with $P(X\le m)\ge\tfrac12$. Since $P(X\le2)<\tfrac12$ and $P(X\le3)>\tfrac12$, the median of $X$ is $3$.

questions.enonce_markdown: A discrete random variable $X$ has probability mass function $f(x)=c(9-x^2)$ for $x=1,2$, $f(x)=c(25-x^2)$ for $x=3,4$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. Find the mean and standard deviation of $X$. *[5 marks]*
A continuous random variable $Y$ has normal distribution with mean $9$ and variance $4$. Given that $P(Y>k) = 0.025$, determine the value of $k$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$Y\sim N(9,\,4)$, so the standard deviation is $\sigma=2$. Standardise with $Z=\dfrac{Y-9}{2}\sim N(0,1)$:

$$P(Y>k) = P\left(Z>\frac{k-9}{2}\right) = 0.025.$$

Hence $P\left(Z\le\dfrac{k-9}{2}\right) = 1-0.025 = 0.975$. From the normal distribution tables, $\Phi(1.96)=0.975$, so

$$\frac{k-9}{2} = 1.96 \;\Longrightarrow\; k = 9 + 2(1.96) = 12.92.$$
